findings.title: Local private backup ownership and temporary destination are still unchecked
findings.resolved_part: Server guard rejects linked, aliased, outside-root, non-directory, foreign-owner and cross-device existing output ancestry; adapter invokes it before and after the unchanged serializer. The ten real server filesystem fixtures passed.
findings.remaining_part: The local D branch only checks resolve equality for D/dest/target. It never checks owner of D or existing/new task descendants. The actual SCP destination is target.name + .partial, which is only checked with exists(); a dangling link can pass that check and the temporary path has no resolve/reparse/owner validation. The ten server fixtures do not exercise Windows destinations.
findings.observed_state: Existing task-owned local ancestors are owned by the current user and have Directory attributes without ReparsePoint. D volume root is SYSTEM-owned, as recorded separately. No recovery round15000 destination exists; no misdirection or disclosure was observed.
findings.requested_resolution: Validate the task private root and each relevant local directory/file, including the exact .partial transfer destination, for expected ownership, containment and links/reparse points before writes; preserve any existing incomplete destination. Apply an explicit volume-root ownership policy rather than demanding the whole D volume be user-owned.

findings.title: Broad failure preservation still excludes some transport and reap paths
findings.resolved_part: CPU dispatch now has a durable exclusive intent before the existing frozen run_supervised call; that supervisor writes child log/resources and final exit/error/cleanup proof in its protected finally path. recorded_remote persists intent and full normal/nonzero/single-timeout/spawn-error synthetic client outcomes and keeps remote outcome unknown until independent server proof.
findings.remaining_part: Initial readiness and final source verification still call session.remote: nonzero exits are truncated to final6000 characters per stream with no actual return code; timeout raises before a durable per-call result. The SCP transfer journal is written only after subprocess.run returns, so spawn/timeout exceptions preserve only the outer traceback. In recorded_remote, a second communicate timeout records streams from the first TimeoutExpired rather than any later partial streams attached to cleanup_error. These branches were reviewed statically and were not injected in this pass.
findings.observed_state: All three documented commands exited0 and all stderr streams were empty. The four prescribed synthetic cases retained intent plus actual outcomes (normal0, nonzero7, timeout1/reaped, spawn no PID/no exit). No real CPU audit or transfer occurred.
findings.requested_resolution: Use durable pre-dispatch and final transport records for every SSH/SCP stage, preserve raw streams and actual code independently of parsing, and preserve the newest available partial streams plus explicit incomplete/reap/remote-unknown status on cleanup failure; do not relaunch uncertain remote work.

evidence_scope: Only the aggregate report and summary are suitable for public copying. Raw streams, process arguments, local ACLs and operational evidence remain local.
environment_scope: Warm metadata tools; no environment rebuild, model load, GPU kernel witness or physical screening claimed.
